primitives.name: Conduct mandate
primitives.desc: Strict deterministic CBOR v1 mandates, domain-separated SHA-256 commitments, allowlist roots and validated payment/egress action digests. Canonical decoding preserves all UTF-8 text including a leading BOM. Schema validity does not establish principal authority. Inputs are copied before validation; identifier limits are UTF-8 byte bounds and payment actions reject zero amounts and unknown fields.

primitives.name: Conduct predicate compiler
primitives.desc: Root-bound mandate compiler emitting a golden-fixture-pinned 12-slot predicate ABI with uint64 action and prior-spend validation. Circuit proof generation and authentication of witness membership/spend are separate obligations.

primitives.name: Conduct runtime guard
primitives.desc: Payment/egress authorization with a trusted guard clock, action times no later than the clock and epoch-aligned spend caps. Accounting state is an explicit constructor input: "fresh" or a replay that must end at the event log's head (count plus a domain-separated SHA-256 chain over canonical event data). Payments require an event sink; the sink contract appends only if the log head still equals the expected previous head (count and hash) and returns the new head, which the guard compares with its own, so a second live guard, a stale restart or a forged replica fails closed against a conforming log (MemoryGuardLog is the reference); the guard trusts the host's log to perform the append and cannot detect a sink that fabricates the head without writing. Trace-safe immutable events are validated before reservation; synchronous enforcement rejects promise sinks and awaited enforcement authorizes only after sink acceptance. processTraceSink records events in a process-trace span and returns the addEvent promise. Hosts own durable conditional-append storage, head custody (separate store, signature or anchor) and all identity, attestation and disclosure checks.

primitives.name: Process trace
primitives.desc: Cryptographic process-trace library: schemas, hashing, v1 Merkle trees and synchronous inclusion proofs, bundles whose span and event IDs are unique and whose public view and top-level model-manifest copies must equal the committed run's (redacted hashes in any order, so every locale's and release's bundles verify), and selective disclosure that reads its input once, recomputes event and span hashes, returns only committed fields, binds full entries to any caller-authenticated leaf hash for their span ID, and verifies membership entries only against caller-authenticated leaf hashes and leaf count passed as own option properties. Concurrent addEvent calls on one run append one at a time, so the rolling hash chains every event, and verifyRollingHash requires seqs 0 to n - 1.

primitives.name: Conduct circuits (prototype)
primitives.desc: Prototype, not deployed, ABI not frozen; no key or proof ships. Compact 0.31.1 conduct verdict: pure evaluate (slice-1 12-slot ABI) and guard_verdict (guard clock), provable check_verdict; inputs unauthenticated, guard_verdict conditional on three guard-state preconditions (D12), assets compared by 248-bit assetTag. Byte-exact openings of guard events and mandate CBOR in exact-length classes: out-of-class bytes refused; chain continuity and anchoring assumed; K carries no authority. The ev_* circuits open a guard event's process-trace preimage (one template of 11 kinds) in 5 compiled classes of 3 kinds, link its hash to the rolling step and disclose its values. The m_* circuits open mandate CBOR to its commitment C and atoms commitment K under the schema rules. The st_* step circuits (10 classes) tie for one event: its recorded decision equals the verdict over its own opened action, the atoms under the K the step discloses, an in-circuit allowlist path from the event's own party, its spend window and a stated prior spend, with the action digest recomputed; verdicts 5 and 7 (non-membership) are refused, never proven. Prior spend, chain continuity, root authenticity and the K weld to a mandate opening are stated assumptions; no cumulative or whole-run claim. Structure audits of verdict, gadgets and generated classes against references from classes.json and the producers; a 501,120-cell order-type differential against the runtime guard; 33 real guard events rendered exactly; class-fit guard sequences through the real guard; every moved witness byte, atom, path entry and window value, and every statement field moved by one, refused by an assert at JS and sampled at ZKIR; mutants killed but one recorded equivalent. Opt-in bench circuits measure variants and the existing span tree (count and index gaps pinned). compile-conduct --check pins ZKIR hashes, k, rows, ops and sources; measure.mjs keys, proves and natively verifies only circuits with installed pinned parameters.

primitives.name: Materios anchor client
primitives.desc: Blob upload through the gateway (body-bound, single-use upload signatures), receipt and anchor submission with bounded WebSocket waits, an exact retry contract (node refusals not-landed, per-block storage reconciliation through one shared recovery reader per provider that disconnect() ends, finalized-storage resolveInclusion, duplicate-free retries, a mortality end computed from the era's own birth block), replacement of a connection that stopped answering, certification polling, Merkle proofs and end-to-end receipt verification against Materios.

primitives.name: Cardano anchor client
primitives.desc: Direct Cardano L1 anchors: Proof-of-Intent label 2222 metadata builders and verifiers, the Materios checkpoint label 8746 record builder and a decoder for both of its mainnet encodings, the end-to-end Materios checkpoint verifier and its Koios source, and a chained submit queue so one wallet never double-spends its own change and each dedupe key is answered by the one tx that reached the chain.

primitives.name: Materios checkpoint anchor verifier
primitives.desc: verifyMateriosCheckpointAnchor proves a certified Materios receipt is in a checkpoint batch anchored on Cardano under label 8746 without trusting the gateway's record: it recomputes the leaf from the receipt's cert hash or the fields that rebuild its Cert, the root through the count-bound rootFromPath (so [a,b,c,c] is not taken for [a,b,c]), the daemon's Python json.dumps(sort_keys) manifest hash and the anchor id, then requires a tx in a block, funded only by caller-pinned anchor wallets in an explicitly pinned record encoding and inclusive Cardano absolute-slot window, whose label-8746 record, in the live worker's detailed-schema encoding or the Lucid-based worker's flat one and refusing any mix or other p/v such as the v:3 finality record, carries the same root, leaf count, manifest and a block range holding the certification, at least 15 confirmations deep by default. It reports the record's chain field and does not compare it: the field is a label that genuine anchors of two windows (1672 live-worker anchors naming the worker's fallback 5663079a, 291 Lucid-worker anchors whose leaves and manifest commit to the previous genesis) get wrong, while the leaf and manifest hash commit to the genesis. It finds the tx by hash or by scanning the pinned wallets from a Cardano height, names the check that refused, and reads Cardano only through an injectable source (createKoiosCheckpointSource, any Koios-compatible baseUrl). Pins are copied before source calls; the exported historical wallet windows are reviewed through 2026-10-24. The Koios source validates absolute slots and refuses repeated pagination entries. Historical dcbor certificates retain their own known chain domain while checkpoint leaves and manifests keep their original commitment genesis. Golden fixtures recorded from Cardano mainnet by scripts/record-materios-checkpoint.mjs.

primitives.name: Compact toolchain installer
primitives.desc: tools/compactc/install.sh installs compactc 0.31.1 (language 0.23.0) for Linux x86_64 and aarch64 and macOS x86_64 and arm64, refusing a release zip or any file inside it whose sha256 differs from compactc.sha256, and installs beside it the ZK public parameters k=13, 14 and 16 and each ledger's DUST spend circuit's prover key, verifier key and zkir (k=13): ledger 8's as circuit generation 9 (dust/9, pinned as midnight-ledger 8.1.3 pins it) and ledger 9's as generation 10 (dust/10, pinned as ledger 9.1.0.0 pins it), each staged under its full path so the two generations' files never overwrite each other, so compactc and zkir find every parameter they need and fetch nothing. It installs only into directories that no one but the caller can write or swap out: every directory above them is owned by the caller or root and closed to group and others, and nothing is installed below a shared sticky directory such as /tmp. An existing install counts only if every file still matches its pin. The one installer for every Compact build in the repo: the registry contract's compile.sh, midnight-prover's circuits, the submitter's DUST spend proofs, CI and the release pack. All downloads are staged and verified before installing files, so a failed download leaves a fresh destination empty.

primitives.name: Orynq anchor registry (Midnight)
primitives.desc: Compact contract (compactc 0.31.1) that records orynq anchors on Midnight with a maintenance authority of committee [], threshold 1, counter 0, so no update can ever apply. anchor(commitment, kind) refuses kind 2; anchor_hiding(attribute) computes a SHA-256 hiding commitment in-circuit from a private opening and binds the attribute to that commitment, not to the trace; neither reads state. Pure circuits author_key, entry_digest, hidden_digest, hiding_commitment and derive_salt are plain SHA-256. compile.sh --check reproduces the committed managed/ byte for byte with the compactc-toolchain compiler. Deployed on Midnight mainnet as registry generation 1 at 438b1ea134e760e8b4e87409d663f36561f15341880c118dc41e4fc2b224c736 by transaction 1bb33baa… in block 3113819, holding FPS's first kind-1 and kind-2 anchors.

primitives.name: GRANDPA finality and strict inclusion verifier
primitives.desc: Decides from untrusted grandpa_proveFinality and chain_getHeader answers (batched JSON-RPC, at most 32 requests a batch, since rpc.mainnet.midnight.network refuses a request body over 8 KiB) whether a block is final, trusting only given checkpoints: it follows each authority set change from the nearest checkpoint below the block (the outgoing set's supermajority-signed justification of a set-change block after the set's start, whose header hashes to it and names the next set in FRNK; forced and delayed changes refused), then checks the finalizing set's justification and the header chain down to the block. Cost is bounded by maxSetChanges (default 2016, six weeks of 30-minute sets, about 6.7 KB each), never by chain age, and each justification's work is linear in its size: non-voters' and repeated precommits are skipped by lookup, only each voter's first two different precommits (told apart by target and signature, as finality-grandpa does) and the commit's lowest voter precommit are Ed25519-verified, and each ancestry header is walked at most once; nothing is refused for its count, since Substrate accepts and serves justifications padded with non-voters' or repeated precommits and repeated ancestry headers. An equivocating voter counts when finality-grandpa's round base, the commit's lowest voter precommit, is signed, lies on the target's chain and is, or through the ancestry headers is an ancestor of, both its precommits, and some voter's precommit is for the target or a descendant; a precommit off that base is set aside where finality-grandpa refuses the whole commit. GRANDPA signs no chain or genesis: a justification that keys holding a supermajority of a set's weight signed under that set id on another GRANDPA chain, an earlier incarnation of the same chain included, verifies here, and the walk then follows that chain's own set changes, so a verdict holds only while more than two thirds of each set's weight is held by honest keys that sign under that set id on this chain alone. One key's precommits from two chains pair into an equivocation only where the commit's lowest precommit is a block both chains share. Inclusion is a strict decode: the ordered-trie (layout V1) extrinsicsRoot of the body and exactly one bare Midnight.send_mn_transaction(tx) extrinsic, never a byte search. Golden vectors from Midnight mainnet and preprod; Materios, also a GRANDPA chain, can verify against it. verifyFinalizedTransaction authenticates arbitrary Midnight transaction bytes, complete inclusion, GRANDPA finality and successful execution from the existing read-RPC transport for reuse by proof presentations.

primitives.name: Signed KNOWN_AUTHORS document
primitives.desc: Signed relay and batch author windows, immutable checkpoint identities and append-only checkpoint prefixes across increasing serials. The first shipped policy pins the historical mainnet relay window, the hosted batch author and the original checkpoint. Defaults strictly verify every shipped document; explicit roots select a separate trust domain while every caller document remains mandatory and strictly verified. Higher serials close author windows, same-serial conflicts fail, and older documents cannot roll back revocation. Ed25519 domain-separated signatures cover exact document strings. Initial custody uses owner-only software keys on operator-approved existing hosts; root signing is separate from the online batch author. Policy text is parsed by the shared strict JSON parser before interpretation, so duplicate decoded keys (escaped aliases included), lone surrogates, a value inside more than 32 containers and numbers without one exact spelling are refused. knownAuthorsSigningSummary and the inspect CLI expose document SHA-256, serial, issued time, author windows and checkpoint authority fingerprints. CLI signing binds the exact inspected digest and requires independently replayed GRANDPA advancement evidence for each appended checkpoint from a current pinned predecessor; bootstrap and root replacement require separate trust review. Neither an RPC authority list nor a self-consistent replacement checkpoint is signing evidence.

primitives.name: Authenticated Midnight checkpoint maintenance
primitives.desc: deriveCheckpointAdvance, verifyCheckpointAdvance and verifyCheckpointAdvanceHistory record and independently replay bounded GRANDPA proof/header transcripts from an existing signed predecessor, binding the network, original root, consecutive sequence, previous digest and exact derived successor. The CLI derives only a fresh runtime/storage-proof-authenticated target and verifies full history offline; it refuses overwriting its input. Authenticated descendants accelerate verification without replacing signed roots or author policy. The private checkpoint-history consumer atomically extends additive follower schema v3 while preserving original policy identity, intermediate checkpoints, coverage, attempts, admissions, fees and retained plans; prefix loss, rollback, forks, missing references and inconsistent restore fail closed. The Woodpecker checkpoint-weekly workflow replays history on PRs without a publication token and derives/replays main-branch candidates before an isolated SHA-pinned builtin-only publisher receives repository-scoped credentials. The publisher opens immutable candidate-specific review PRs, preserving current-main history and never merging or force-updating main. The committed mainnet history contains an independently replayed successor through finalized block 3186840 with authenticated chain time 2026-10-26T19:13:00Z; this evidence does not establish a configured recurring cron/credential, a remotely accepted maintenance proposal or host rollout. Activation requires operator setup of the weekly schedule/token, maintainer review and coherent state backup/history install with a v3-capable restart. Bounds are 64 MiB per artifact, 4096 artifacts/512 MiB retained history and 64 MiB publisher bundles; limits hold maintenance for review without pruning evidence.

primitives.name: Midnight anchor toolkit
primitives.desc: Explicit RPC-only verification accepts transaction block hints, proves full execution and Timestamp.Now from finalized storage proofs under the runtime the parent state selects (its :pending_code when present, with absence proven otherwise, else its :code; runtime 1000300 or 2001100 by code hash) and that runtime's SHA256-pinned metadata, and caches verified batch sets within source/registry/checkpoint/finality policy while rechecking current batch-author windows. Kind-3 certified receipt batch sets and portable receipt proofs bind the expected content, Materios genesis, certificate format, shape-bound tree, census manifest and member set to a finalized Midnight transaction by a known batch author. verifyBatchSet returns stored verification facts; authorStatusAt revalidates a window without chain I/O. verifyMidnightAnchor checks an anchor from the transaction's own bytes: hash binding first, then exactly one registry call whose guaranteed transcript equals the compiled circuits' op for op, the node's block (hash, header, extrinsicsRoot, known runtime, strict send_mn_transaction inclusion), GRANDPA finality from a signed or caller checkpoint, the registry's pinned deploy verified the same way, the request's expectation (or kind "any", which matches nothing and reports the anchor) and the author: the key the caller pins (expectedAuthor; an anchor another key wrote is invalid, author mismatch, naming both keys) or a KNOWN_AUTHORS author window; a result takes its most severe failed check's status (invalid, conflict, unavailable, unverified-finality, unauthenticated, author-revoked, in that order), or valid, which exists only at consensus-verified assurance; verifiedFields name only what the commitment binds (kind 2: committedAttribute, never the trace). verifyReport makes a result printable for a terminal or a model: no finality checkpoint, source-shaped text stripped of control, format and unassigned characters and cut at 300 characters, a block hash that is not one dropped. findMidnightAnchors lists an author set's anchor candidates in a window of at most 20,000 blocks from the indexer's contractActions subscription (WebSocket, credential in a header), decoding each from its own bytes, bounded by maxActions with a resumable cursor. Its explicit indexer-reported assurance and authorStatus at each reported height distinguish candidates and indexer completion from consensus verification or proof of chain-wide completeness. It also computes commitments with the compiled contract's own pure circuits (entryCommitment, hiddenDigest, hidingCommitment, deriveSalt, authorKey), writes (wholly and flushed to disk, or not at all) and reads random author key files only their owner can read, writes random salt key files published only by their id (saltKeyId), and user key files (orynq-midnight-user-key/v1: author secret and salt key) whose reader refuses a bare service author key file, lists the deployed registry generations per network (generation 1 on mainnet at 438b1ea1…, deployed by 1bb33baa… in block 3113819; none on preprod) with their pinned verifier keys and runtime height spans (generation 1: 1000300 for 3113819 through 3346138, 2001100 from 3346139; registryRuntimeAllows binds an anchor block's runtime to its height), names the runtime that executes the block after a given header from that header's own state, :pending_code when present and :code otherwise, through a read proof mapped by code hash and refused outside the runtime table (runtimeAfter), reads a Midnight indexer and node through midnightSource (its indexer also names its block at a height, blockAt, which the wallet's liveness check compares with the node's; Blockfrost endpoints with the project id read from an owner-only file, refused unless shaped like a project id so no other secret is sent as one, and kept out of every error, or a configured indexer and node URL through sourceEndpoints; source identities and block metadata are validated, provider error bodies and reasons are withheld, diagnostics are printable and bounded, a node's JSON-RPC error is a NodeError naming only the method and numeric code, and a batch is refused at its first failed request), reads a contract's state at a block or null where none is (contractStateOnNode normalizes null and empty bytes; midnight-node 2.x -32602 counts as absent only after a valid 33-byte zswap-root read for the same block in the configured node's batched response, since an unavailable ledger can return the same code; unknown absence errors fail closed), builds registry calls for a given network from the compiled circuits (unprovenRegistryCall): a ledger 8 transaction[v9] against the ledger 8 state, or against the contract-state[v8] a ledger 9 network holds a ledger 9 transaction[v12] carrying the ledger 8 circuit's call, partitioned with the chain's ledger 9 parameters (ledgerParametersIn; midnightSource's indexer reads the head block's), with circuit outputs, transcript partition and transaction shape pinned against midnight-js 5's retained ledger 8 call path, recorded by tools/midnight-js-oracle, serves each file of the committed build only while it matches contract/HASHES.txt (compiledContractFile), frames a transaction as the bare Midnight.send_mn_transaction extrinsic a node accepts (midnightExtrinsic, the inverse of the strict inclusion decode), and builds the registry's exact deploy state from the compiled constructor and the sha256-pinned verifier keys, reads every transaction and contract state with the ledger its header tag names (ledger 8 for transaction[v9] and contract-state[v6], ledger 9 for transaction[v12] and contract-state[v8], any other tag refused; registryState returns the immutable registry's state and registryVerifierKeysIn its verifier key hashes from either; decodeTransaction reads final bytes by tag, and assertTransactionRuntime binds a transaction to the runtime that executed it, since ledger 8 bytes relabelled transaction[v12] decode under ledger 9 as another transaction: verifyMidnightAnchor's transaction-ledger check and verifyFinalizedTransaction, which returns the executing runtime, refuse a transaction outside its block runtime's ledger), and refuses anything else: assertImmutableAuthority (committee [], threshold 1, counter 0), assertRegistryState (operations, canonical verifier keys, schema) and assertRegistryDeployBytes, which decodes the exact deploy bytes before or after proving and requires the initial state byte for byte. Public on npm. KNOWN_AUTHORS ships the signed serial-1 mainnet relay and hosted batch windows with the original GRANDPA checkpoint. Callers may select explicit trust domains or pin authors and checkpoints; anchors outside an authorized window remain refused. The suite replays FPS's two mainnet anchors and their negative controls (wrong or no author key, a commitment or attribute one bit off, an unpinned registry address, another contract's call), recorded node-only through rpc.mainnet.midnight.network by scripts/mainnet-anchors.mjs, which also runs from an installed tarball. The shared nodeRefusal decoder recognizes typed redacted source errors and legacy JSON submission refusals; only canonical numeric custom transaction codes survive source redaction.

primitives.name: Write-ahead anchor submission journal
primitives.desc: SQLite (node:sqlite) write-ahead journal exported as anchors-midnight/journal: one live attempt per semantic anchor key, with final bytes and their computed hash persisted before broadcast. Uncertain delivery resumes identical bytes, and a caller naming its confirmed transaction never sends a competing live row. Before broadcast, the journal records a canonical finalized scan boundary. journal-chain scans configured-node finalized block bodies from that boundary in bounded reconciles (at most 128 blocks and 30 seconds), validating pinned genesis, header hashes, parent links and body roots, and detects either the exact transaction or the same semantic anchor inside merged transactions. Final bytes are read with the ledger their header names (transaction[v9] with ledger 8, [v12] with ledger 9), so a row's hash is always its own ledger's, and a scanned block carrying a transaction its runtime's ledger does not read is a source conflict that settles nothing. Canonical inclusion of a guaranteed anchor is landed even when the indexer reports PARTIAL; SUCCESS, FAILURE, PARTIAL or a missing indexer result alone never frees an anchor key. Retirement requires complete absence through the same finalized block whose node Timestamp.Now exceeds every encoded intent TTL plus the margin (five minutes by default). A deploy additionally needs validated ledger-root and contract-state absence at that block. Legacy attempts without a scan boundary remain held unless positive inclusion is found. Each view and settlement is network-bound. This recovery path trusts the configured pinned-genesis node's canonical finalized view; it does not independently prove GRANDPA finality, and jointly malicious node/indexer answers are outside that assumption. Production operator completion separately requires consensus-verified known-author evidence. Finalized deploy readback requires exact bytes, and relocation/orphan metadata follows the configured canonical chain. The journal retains exact bytes, payer, scan progress and live key identity across restarts; reconcile and relocate prepare and broadcast nothing. The DB, WAL and SHM are owner-only; writes serialize within and across processes. Missing, inconsistent or unknown legacy state remains held for recovery.

primitives.name: Midnight anchor submitter
primitives.desc: Canonical kind-3 receipt batch plans recompute member identities and commitment labels. Batch authors write only kind3; relays only1/2; retired author identities are refused on every network. Confirmation summaries bind the commitment, genesis and member count; legacy per-intent approvals refuse standing batch plans. Deploys the immutable orynq-anchor-registry and writes anchors to it. openWallet runs a wallet-sdk 2.0.0 WalletFacade (facade 5.0.0, HD account 0 index 0) that refuses a mnemonic deriving other than the recorded addresses and pays fees from DUST only. Its sub-wallets follow V9NativeForkSchedule (MIDNIGHT_FORKS: ledger 8 variants below protocol version 2000000, ledger 9 from it), and payFee refuses a transaction of another ledger than the one the wallet acts at. Every wallet connection runs through the credential relay: the SDK gets no relayURL or nodeClientConnection, so it dials no node and runs no liveness probe of its own, openWallet refuses an indexer whose genesis block is not the node's, and payFee checks liveness itself through the source's credentialed transport (indexer head within 10 blocks of the node's finalized block, and the same block at the lower of the two heads, read from the indexer by height with blockAt when it is ahead; assertIndexerLive), paying nothing otherwise. DUST stays under the journal's custody: the facade's lifecycle service, which would free DUST on its own clock once a TTL passes or on a reported failure, is replaced by journalCustodyLifecycle, which records and frees nothing. Both variants take DUST coins largest first (largestCoinFirst) instead of the SDK's smallest first, which spent every coin too small to pay alone on every fee, 1.7x to 3.3x the fee on wallet-sdk 1.x's simulator. Every fee carries at least 1 SPECK of overhead (openWallet refuses less), so every fee carries a DUST spend. The SDK dates each spend at a block whose DUST roots the wallet's trees hold, and refuses a spend whose date plus the grace period would not outlast the TTL. The wallet proves in a worker thread with zkir-v2 2.2.0 from sha256-pinned key material: registry circuits from the committed build, and the k=13/14 parameters and each ledger's DUST spend (dust/9 for ledger 8, dust/10 for ledger 9) from the installer's directory, with nothing fetched. It applies the indexer's events to the shielded and DUST wallets in groups of up to 1000, flushing partial groups after 1 ms (with the SDK's default of 10, a sync from genesis spent more than half its time on per-batch work; on preprod, 1000 applied DUST events more than twice as fast to the same state). It saves and restores its sync state in an owner-only file tagged orynq-midnight-wallet-state/wallet-sdk-2 and bound to the wallet, the network and the indexer it was synced from. A format-less wallet-sdk 1.x file is moved aside to <file>.wallet-sdk-1, never over an earlier one, and the wallet syncs from genesis, but only once no journal the caller names (journals) holds a pending fee of the wallet within its TTL plus the journal's margin, since a genesis sync offers that fee's DUST again; an open naming no journal leaves the file. The mainnet scripts and the standing service share one wallet and state file and each open it with MAINNET_WALLET_JOURNALS (src/mainnet-state.ts: deploy, anchors, proof release and standing attempts journals; a mainnet standing state root outside it is refused, as is a mainnet standing wallet.state other than the shared state file, MAINNET_WALLET_STATE), and the rehearsal's run and crash drill with rehearsalWalletJournals. The file is replaced only once all three sub-wallets serialized and that save's own new file is wholly written and flushed to disk (each save's file is named for its process and a random suffix, and an open removes one whose process died). Only a state each sub-wallet reads back with the SDK's own deserializer is installed, and one wallet's saves run one at a time. An open refuses a state file a sub-wallet does not read back, naming the file and what the SDK said, never the state. A failed save is returned as a value, never thrown, so the next open resumes from the last good save. syncWithCheckpoints waits for the sync, writing progress lines (applied and highest index per sub-wallet, connected and synced flags) as it starts, every minute and once synced, and saving the state every five minutes (spaced so saves, which read the DUST state back, take at most a tenth of the wait), once synced and once more when the wait times out or fails, frees exactly the DUST a fee spent when the node refuses the first delivery of bytes it balanced or a caller discards bytes never handed to a node, never sending those bytes again, and otherwise holds that DUST until the bytes land or the ledger's grace period ends; balances a fee only once the DUST sync has applied every event the indexer's last message announced (payFee waits up to two minutes, then fails with the sync's progress); chooses its endpoints by network (networkEndpoints: Blockfrost on mainnet and preprod alike, refusing to start without a project id file, since Midnight retired its hosted mainnet endpoints and its hosted preprod node refuses JSON-RPC request bodies over about 7 KB, smaller than any deploy or anchor), and reaches Blockfrost through a loopback relay that adds the project-id header so the credential never sits in a URL the SDK logs. registryDeployer prepares the final balanced bytes, refuses them unless they deploy exactly the registry's initial state, and submits them through the write-ahead journal at most once per network, after settling any journalled deploy from the chain (one the node-confirmed chain time has carried past its TTL unseen no longer blocks a new one, unless the node at that block holds a contract at the address its bytes deploy, which lands it however far the indexer's lookup lags; the journal keeps that rule for every reconcile, so an operator sharing the journal file keeps it too, and settles a row only from a chain view of its own network, so a deployer or operator of another network sharing the file never settles the deploy) and checking again that the bytes it sends are that deploy and hash to the confirmed transaction hash, and journalled() returns the deploy the journal still holds, rebuilt from its journalled bytes, with the wallet that paid it and whether chain time is past its TTL, so a caller that failed between broadcast and readback resumes that deploy instead of preparing one the journal would refuse; bytes past their TTL, or that journalled() marked expired, are never sent again (submit waits until the chain lands or retires them), new bytes leave only while chain time is known and short of their TTL, so bytes confirmed after it, however long the prompt waited, are discarded unsent, while the node lacks the indexer's newest block, so that chain time is unknown, submit refuses bytes no send of which returned, a resumed deploy the chain retired is refused as expired, and a submit whose key another deployer journalled first refuses and discards its own bytes, sending nothing (journalOnce binds the journal to the confirmed transaction hash, so the other deployer's row comes back unsent); registryOperator writes kind-1 anchor and kind-2 anchor_hiding calls under an author key read only from a 0600 file (salts derived from a salt key read once when the operator is made, openings returned only to the caller), checks the final bytes decode to exactly the intended anchor before broadcast, and in two steps for a human to confirm (prepare or journalled(), then submit through confirmedSends, the deployer's at-most-once confirmed send: bytes that do not carry exactly the confirmed anchor or hash to the confirmed transaction are refused, a journalled attempt resumes, bytes past their TTL are never sent again, another attempt's bytes are discarded unsent), broadcasts the bare Midnight.send_mn_transaction over JSON-RPC (nodeRefusal tells the node's own JSON-RPC refusal, with its code, from a transport failure that may have delivered the bytes), and waits by txHash. registryStateOnNode reads through the validated contract-state helper; deployment settlement and expiry use pinned-node finalized observations, with unknown absence or time held rather than guessed. Every submission first checks the runtime of the block a transaction can land in, the block after the node's best, read from the code in the best block's own state through a read proof (runtimeAfter: :pending_code when set_code left one, else :code; unknown code refused), since the node's runtime version reports :code alone and so names the old runtime at a set_code block, and builds for its ledger: under 1000300 a ledger 8 transaction[v9], under 2001100 a ledger 9 transaction[v12] carrying the ledger 8 registry circuit's call, partitioned with the indexer head's ledger 9 parameters; for a pinned registry generation the runtime must be the one that generation runs at that next block (runtimeAllowedAt). Confirmed bytes of another ledger than the node now runs are refused unsent (assertBuiltFor), and every send, a journalled row's resend included, checks the node's current runtime at the last send boundary, retaining the row unsent with its DUST held. assertKnownRuntime takes the runtimes its caller builds for, with no default: registryDeployer and proofReleaseOperator, whose builders are ledger 8's, admit only 1000300 (LEDGER8_RUNTIMES), so under 2001100 neither builds, pays for, describes a journalled row as sendable, nor sends anything. A ledger 9 call's parameters must come from a block the node holds under the hash the indexer gives, and that ran the call's runtime. Ledger 9 final bytes must pass ledger 9's time-to-dismiss check under those parameters, or are refused with TimeToDismissError naming their DUST spends and their DUST freed (midnight-ledger#838: a fee paid with one DUST spend can cross the allowance where zero or two stay inside it). openWallet pays ledger 9 fees, and provingService proves either ledger's transactions. At mainnet's ledger 9 prices (block 3350170) an anchor's fee is about 0.15 DUST before its own DUST spend, above the standing service's caps of 0.01 DUST a transaction and 0.1 DUST a day. assertChainIdentity also accepts runtime 2001100 with ledger 9, reading the node's tagged ledger version (crate-ledger-<version>, with its revision), and refuses a runtime whose ledger major is not the one the node reports. scripts/deploy-mainnet.ts is the fail-closed mainnet preflight (chain name and genesis, runtime, recorded wallet, a DUST floor applied before preparing fresh bytes, exact summary naming the wallet that paid) that sends only after a token bound to the bytes' transaction hash is typed at an interactive terminal, in a process without Claude Code or Codex environment, and resumes the deploy its journal still holds (journalled()) instead of preparing another, re-showing it marked as resumed and sending nothing before the same token is typed, and closing the journal and the wallet on every way out: an accident guard under the ship-now decision, which a process running as deci passes by dropping that environment and driving a pseudo-terminal; the custody boundary is the planned separate-uid or FIDO2 signer. Both mainnet scripts sync the wallet from one shared owner-only state file (~/.local/state/orynq-midnight/mainnet-wallet.state.json, --wallet-state, in a directory only its owner can enter) through syncWithCheckpoints with a three-hour timeout, so a sync that times out or fails is resumed by the next run of either. scripts/anchor-mainnet.ts writes the anchors a strict plan names (readAnchorPlan: registry plus ordered kind-1 and kind-2 entries, unknown fields refused) behind the same gates and code (scripts/mainnet-session.ts), refusing a plan before the chain is read, a registry that is not FPS's (assertFpsRegistry: one MIDNIGHT_REGISTRIES pins, or the one whose deploy deploy-mainnet's journal holds landed, so the same immutable registry deployed by anyone else is refused) before the chain is read, and a registry the node does not hold as exactly the immutable registry before any wallet or key, sends each anchor only after ANCHOR and its transaction hash's first 16 hex characters are typed, requires each completion to match the final bytes and block and pass valid, consensus-verified, known-author public verification (where that chain holds another block than the journal cached, registryOperator.relocate settles the anchor afresh from the chain: into the block it landed in since, or out of the journal once past its TTL unseen, so the anchor key never sticks), and adds public data only after that verification to an owner-only results file under a bounded cross-process read/write/rename lock, so a row another run recorded meanwhile is kept, skipping recorded entries on a rerun and at append time (a conflicting transaction for the same label is refused); kind-1 summaries show normalized root, manifest and Merkle hashes, while kind-2 openings stay private, and plan, results and wallet-record JSON parse errors never quote file contents; both scripts refuse a flag given twice or followed by another flag instead of its value, and report a wallet that fails to close after the run's own failure. On mainnet registryOperator loads only the FPS mainnet author key and salt key (MAINNET_AUTHOR_KEYS, MAINNET_SALT_KEY_IDS), refusing any other by identity when it is made, before anything is prepared, so a wrong key file never authors an FPS anchor; off mainnet it refuses those keys by identity wherever the file lives, and it and openWallet refuse any key or mnemonic path inside ~/.secrets/orynq-midnight-mainnet, however the path reaches it. Private: not published to npm. Wallet-state parse failures name the file and recovery action without quoting its contents; network and indexer mismatch diagnostics also omit saved values. The mainnet scripts apply the DUST floor only before preparing fresh bytes: journalled bytes already carry their fee, including an unsent attempt whose fee coin stays held after restoring the wallet. A floor refusal explains when an unspent held coin becomes available after wallet sync passes the spend ctime plus the ledger grace period. Every operator anchor, hiding anchor, batch, submit and relocation completion requires the real verifier's exact transaction/network/registry/call/block result at valid consensus-verified assurance with a known signed-policy author; typed custom-trust verification must satisfy the same full-report checks. The accepted report is retained for CLI output. Preparation snapshots bytes, TTL and semantic fields before async work and refuses additional contract actions or non-DUST offers. Author/network identity binds to one canonical journal path and inode in the operating-system account's owner-only namespace, independent of HOME, wallet path or copied key files; a missing, replaced or different journal is refused. A typed custom custody namespace exists without a CLI or environment override. Same-UID deliberate edits remain outside this accident guard and require separate signer custody to prevent. Largest-first coin order and fee reverts are tested on wallet-sdk 2.0.0's ledger 9 simulator; new live mainnet fee measurements are not claimed. Provider-derived summaries and failures omit unvalidated chain/runtime/ledger text, and interrupted confirmation reads decline without a send. Result updates hold a stable owner-only inode with Linux /usr/bin/flock inherited through a parent descriptor; the kernel retains the lock after the acquiring utility exits and releases it on process death, without stale-PID unlink recovery. Repeated discard is a no-op for transaction hashes whose DUST this wallet already freed. The prepared proof-release window disables the standing service across reboots, recovers the same intent/journal after interruption under existing approval and retirement guards, and re-enables it only after reconciliation and wallet close.

primitives.name: Midnight preprod rehearsal and evidence gate
primitives.desc: The Midnight submitter's preprod rehearsal, committed so its evidence is reproducible. bundles.ts traces real read-only processes into process-trace bundles (entries via anchors-cardano); run.ts and crash.ts, on preprod test tokens only, deploy the registry (resuming the deploy its journal holds, so a run that fails between broadcast and readback leaves the next run that deploy to finish, never a second) and write kind-1 and kind-2 anchors, a same-block pair from two wallets, three maintenance updates the node must refuse, a SIGKILL drill on each journal crash window and a KNOWN_AUTHORS rotation and revocation, recording every wallet state save (after sync and at close) without letting a failed one fail a phase, and every node refusal of an anchor's bytes (anchorRefusals: label, transaction, code and data, time) before the error leaves the phase. verify-all.mjs verifies every recorded anchor, and the absence of every refused maintenance transaction, through Blockfrost from a separate process that loads the verify package only as npm installed it from a packed tarball beside it whose integrity still matches npm's record, and opens KNOWN_AUTHORS documents forged from serial 3. gate.mjs decides what the evidence pack may claim: every anchor a distinct transaction of kind 1 or 2, valid at consensus-verified for its recorded hash and commitment; each crash window's kill mode, words and journal behaviour; the same-block pair in one block as the verifier reads it; each maintenance update refused with exactly JSON-RPC 1010 Invalid Transaction and the maintenance authority's own code (Custom error 136 ThresholdMissed for the unsigned update, 134 KeyNotInCommittee for the stranger-signed ones) and unknown to both indexers; the rotation verdict matrix; each forged document refused by the check it targets (Ed25519 verification for the two under the trust root's key), with a control that opens it under the stranger; a drill trust root the package does not ship; each verifier negative failing for its expected check; and each recorded anchor refusal followed by another transaction for its label that landed and was recorded after it. compose.ts writes the pack only when the gate passes, the journals' landed transactions equal the recorded anchors, every kind-2 opening recomputes the commitment the verifier read and a privacy scan finds no window of any secret, carries each accepted anchor refusal beside the transaction that landed for its label, and discloses every crash-drill attempt that aborted before any kill point, archived unmodified with a sha256sum manifest, refusing an archive whose files differ from or are missing in its manifest and a partial drill archived as aborted; the README maps every statement to its check. record-golden.ts records the verifier's Blockfrost reads of three of its anchors (a valid kind 1, a valid kind 2, the revoked key's author-revoked anchor), which anchors-midnight's suite replays to the recorded verdicts check for check. The offline suite, which also runs run.ts's deploy and kind1 phases in their own processes over a replaced wallet, prover and chain with one run failed at a chosen step, runs in CI; the network steps run by hand after the faucet (README runbook).

primitives.name: Midnight mainnet approval runner
primitives.desc: Runs the orynq-anchor-registry deploy and the anchors into it on Midnight mainnet unattended once deci approves the exact intent in chat: systemd user units (orynq-midnight-runner@<id>.service, started by a dispatch service that a path unit on the approvals directory and a 15-minute timer trigger) run the reviewed scripts/deploy-mainnet.ts and scripts/anchor-mainnet.ts under util-linux script and a shared flock execution lock, and type each confirmation token only when the tool's summary matches the intent fact by fact (confirm.ts, available to the terminal wrappers: network, authority, verifier keys, payer and fee cap for a deploy; label, kind, registry, hashes, the commitment entryCommitment derives for kind 1, the attribute for kind 2, author key, payer and fee cap for an anchor; a token naming the summarized transaction), and otherwise answer NO. The gate (gate.ts) admits an intent only while an approval written after deci's chat approval names its sha256 (compact JSON, keys as written; its first 8 hex are the id), was given by deci in chat, has not expired (24 hours at most) and has not been used, its action and every fact limits.json pins are allowlisted (the exact immutable registry deploy; anchors into the registry deploy-mainnet's journal holds landed, from a plan whose sha256 and entries match), its fee cap is within the per-transaction cap (0.01 DUST) and other intents' DUST reservations for the rolling 24-hour window plus its maximum stays within the daily cap (0.1); it checks again at every prompt, with at most three confirmations per transaction, other bytes for a transaction only once the tool's write-ahead journal explicitly holds every earlier set failed; a missing journal or lost row requires recovery and cannot prove non-submission. Same-byte retries remain possible. Every transaction hash is counted once against the daily cap at the maximum fee recorded for it, including zero-fee records. Failures other than a NO are retried with backoff until the approval expires, an attempt whose exit status the shell never reported included (util-linux script exits 0 when a stray SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGQUIT ends it, so only the tool's own status, reported on a descriptor the tool does not hold, finishes a run), the tools resuming the wallet sync from their saved state; anchors authorized before the deploy wait for the journal's landed deploy and get their plan written from the template (landedRegistryDeploy, fillPlan). run and dispatch refuse Claude Code or Codex environment, and run only as the unit systemd started (INVOCATION_ID). Status files, an append-only audit log, a one-line status command and systemd-analyze-verified units; a guardrail against mistakes and drift, not a custody boundary, since every agent on the host runs as the same user. The full intent and approval digests stay pinned throughout the run. The anchor tool checks --plan-sha256 against the same bytes it parses, including hidden entry inputs. Each attempt confirms each item once; every NO, a NO to a prompt for the other action included, is in the audit log, flushed, before the tool reads it, and is terminal for its approval across interruptions. NO audit records carry the pinned approval digest; admission and dispatch recover them even without a status snapshot or used marker. Approval times must end in Z or a ±hh:mm offset, since Date.parse reads a time without one in the runner's time zone; the gate refuses one without. An approval's digest is the sha256 of its six values with each time as the instant it names, so a used approval rewritten with other whitespace, key order or offset stays used in every time zone. A summary's validity deadline and the audit's confirmation times without an offset get NO and a refusal. Used markers are scoped to the consumed approval digest, so stopping an old run does not consume a replacement approval. Legacy markers and terminal records without an approval identity keep the intent closed. Confirmation audit records include approval digests, are flushed before a token is sent, and restore confirmation counts when status is lost. Status and used markers are flushed with their directory entries. The execution lock serializes wallet access and daily-cap decisions, and resumed bytes whose reservation aged out need fresh daily headroom. Confirmation refuses a validity deadline more than one hour ahead. Each reservation lasts until 24 hours after the later of confirmation and its bounded deadline; historical audit deadlines are capped at one hour after confirmation so injected dates cannot reserve capacity forever. Prompt parsing consumes one complete summary per token, refuses duplicate headers or fields, missing required fields and interleaved/control text, caps retained summary context at 64 KiB and one attempt at 128 prompts, and preserves split progress lines in a bounded 4 KiB status buffer while the full log remains on disk. A separate proof-release action authorizes only the pinned immutable proof contract deploy and one fixed synthetic capability and rolling demonstration, preserving the existing fee, daily, expiry and single-use gates. Its own journal binds calls to the landed proof deployment. The standing anchor policy does not authorize proof relay spending. Proof summaries use an action-specific strict field set; proof-call journal keys require exact inclusion. The operator stops the standing service for the shared-lock release window and restarts it after the runner exits.

primitives.name: Tool-call receipts
primitives.desc: Verifiable tool-call receipts with RFC 9421, webhook-signature and JWS verifiers for the process-trace SDK.

primitives.name: Materios x402 payer
primitives.desc: Materios-native sr25519 x402 payer with api-key passthrough for the Materios billing gateway.

primitives.name: Orynq observe
primitives.desc: SDK for publishing attested AI-model behaviour observations to a chain-anchored public registry.

primitives.name: Orynq MCP server
primitives.desc: MCP server exposing process tracing, Cardano and Materios anchoring and verification as agent tools. verify_midnight_anchor (read-only) verifies a Midnight anchor with anchors-midnight, an optional peer dependency loaded on first use (without it the server starts and the tool returns an error naming the package), and returns its verifyReport; its schema is strict (txHash, network, at most one of entry, commitment or attribute), so a model can pass it no trust key, file or URL; author trust comes only from the server's signed KNOWN_AUTHORS policy, and the source comes from the server's environment as a file path or URLs. There is no Midnight anchoring tool and no tool takes a Flux Point Studios key: anchoring with the user's own key goes through the quickstart CLI's terminal confirmation. Adds verify_midnight_receipt for caller-bound genesis, receipt, content and certificate identities, using dedicated explicit read-only proof endpoints and bounded resumable discovery. Valid evidence includes a portable proof; unresolved/exhausted hints never prove absence. Optional older peers receive an actionable upgrade error.

primitives.name: Dual-protocol payment layer
primitives.desc: Flux 402 and x402 commerce layer: core types, auto-pay client, server middleware, transports and Cardano/EVM payers.

primitives.name: PoI attestor backends
primitives.desc: TEE attestation types, policy helpers and backend scaffolding. Nitro and SEV-SNP verification fail closed as unavailable; no bundled backend authenticates hardware evidence.

primitives.name: Flight recorder
primitives.desc: Streaming flight recorder with chunking, compression and encryption for long-running traces, and chunk Merkle proofs verified against an authenticated leaf count.

primitives.name: Storage adapters
primitives.desc: IPFS, S3 and Arweave storage backends for trace payloads.

primitives.name: Orynq quickstart
primitives.desc: Solo-developer quickstart: generates an identity, faucet-drips MATRA and anchors a first trace in minutes. For Midnight, with anchors-midnight installed as an optional peer dependency (without it the Midnight commands exit 1 naming it): `orynq verify midnight <txHash|bundle>` verifies an anchor read-only and prints its status, assurance, author, matched fields and every check (Blockfrost project id file or any indexer and node URL); `orynq keys init midnight` writes the user's own key file; `orynq anchor midnight` plans an anchor with that key only, refusing bare service key files and every KNOWN_AUTHORS key, as a dry run unless a signed policy is available and --submit is confirmed at a TTY by typing the commitment's first 8 characters (no registry or submitter in this build, so it stops before asking). Adds orynq verify midnight-receipt with expected genesis/content/certificate identities, explicit new proof endpoints, bounded regular-file continuations and JSON portable evidence. Exit0 requires valid consensus-verified coverage; unresolved remains exit1 without an absence claim. Bundle and key JSON failures identify the file and recovery action without quoting parser input or private file contents.

primitives.name: Midnight prover
primitives.desc: Local Compact capability and exact rolling proofs plus immutable keyed on-chain presentations, caller-wallet post and checkpoint-rooted verifyPosted using authenticated execution. Compiled ledger-8 keys and initial state are pinned and ship in npm. Mainnet-deployed on 2026-10-27: the immutable deployment and both synthetic presentations have independent fresh-consumer consensus-verified receipts. PROOF_DEPLOYMENTS exports deeply frozen mainnet and preprod addresses, deployment transaction hashes and block hints, code hashes and initial-state digests. Legacy publication is explicitly simulation-only; simulation disclosure proofs that carry a span without its events, or events without their span, never verify and are reported unbound, naming only the caller-authenticated span their Merkle path proves, and every disclosure is bound to the caller's expected Merkle root whenever leaf hashes or a leaf count are given. Each call reads current state, budgets gas with headroom. Malformed event digests produce value-free errors; verification trust roots bind their genesis. Verification refuses unknown network labels and requires both authenticated transactions to encode the requested network. Direct posting retries only definitive node transcript refusals (1010/custom 104) or local pre-submission gas exhaustion, at most three attempts, with ambiguous sends preserved.

primitives.name: Compute meter SDK
primitives.desc: Client for emitting compute-metering records into the Materios billing pipeline.

primitives.name: OpenClaw recorder
primitives.desc: Daemon and CLI that tail OpenClaw agent sessions into process-trace bundles and anchor each bundle once, polling until confirmed

primitives.name: PoI anchor worker
primitives.desc: HTTP service behind t-backend that anchors process-trace manifests to Cardano under label 2222 from one wallet, chaining bursts through the anchors-cardano submit queue, answering a request identical to one in flight or recently landed with that tx (never one anchoring different content), rejecting malformed hashes with 400, and shedding load with 503 when the queue is full.

primitives.name: npm release
primitives.desc: The CLI library exports createProgram and a manifest-derived VERSION without executing; the separate poi bin preserves command behavior, with built ESM and CJS import regressions. Dependency tests require patched Zod, body-parser, Hono, Vitest mocker, Fastify and IPv6 address parsing releases; MCP metadata schemas accept Zod 4 records. Post-publication probes require the exact version in npm's installation metadata and revalidate the installer cache; propagation and transient ECONNRESET or UND_ERR_SOCKET failures share the existing visibility attempt/delay budget. Exhaustion, malformed metadata, nontransient errors and failed installs still fail. Publishes every workspace package version npm lacks on a push to main: a token-less step installs, runs release-guard (refuses a public package with a runtime dependency on a private one, named directly, through an npm: or workspace: alias or by a workspace: path resolved through symlinks, or on a local path (link:, file: or bare) or a spec npm-package-arg cannot classify, a version npm would record differently, and a version below one npm already has by npm's semver order, prereleases included), then builds and packs them (scripts/pack-unpublished.mjs, the choice changeset publish makes); only the digest-pinned npm-publish plugin, named by the npm_token secret's image filter, holds the token; post-publish-check then installs each published version from npm, alone and together, imports it and requires one copy of each WASM singleton. CI dry-runs changeset version in isolated manifest copies with a minor probe for each private package and refuses public major bumps.

primitives.name: Strict JSON parser
primitives.desc: parseStrictJson(text, maxBytes, maxValues?) gives every accepted text exactly one decoded meaning: it refuses text over the byte limit (UTF-8), text holding more than maxValues values (every container, string, number and literal counts, keys do not; unbounded when omitted), duplicate decoded object keys including escaped spellings, lone surrogates in keys or values, any value enclosed by more than 32 containers (the top-level value is enclosed by none, as in conduct's CBOR decoder), integers beyond ±2^53 (judged on the digits, not the rounded double) and integers spelled with a fraction, exponent or minus zero; non-integral numbers pass through for the caller's schema. Nesting and values are judged by one scan before JSON.parse, so a 16 MiB nesting bomb or a 16 MiB text of empty containers, numbers or members over the value bound is refused without allocating; the token checks after JSON.parse are a single charCode pass. Each limit must be a non-negative integer or Infinity, else TypeError, since a NaN limit would bound nothing. Refusals are StrictJsonError with a code and a fixed message that never quotes the input.

primitives.name: Credential broker wire contract
primitives.desc: Public subpath @fluxpointstudios/orynq-sdk-core/broker-wire, imported at runtime by the private broker, whose serveMux speaks this mux to the Linux orynq-socket-frontend and the Windows sidecar, and by the public Windows host package, whose spawnPipeFrontend refuses an admitted SID that isAccountSid refuses before spawning the sidecar. parsePeer accepts exactly {os:'linux', uid, gid, pidHint, cgroup} or {os:'windows', sid, logonLuid, tsSessionId, integrityRid, pidHint}, refusing unknown or missing keys and reading each own property once (an accessor, a symbol key or a non-enumerable key is refused, so the peer it returns is the one it checked): uid, gid, tsSessionId and integrityRid u32 numbers, pidHint u32 or null, cgroup an absolute cgroup v2 path (non-empty components, no NUL or newline, at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes), sid any SID as ConvertSidToStringSidW spells it (S-1-, a decimal authority below 2^32 and 1 to 15 decimal u32 sub-authorities, no leading zeros), since the Windows sidecar's DACL admits SYSTEM (S-1-5-18) and its exact peer must decode, logonLuid a canonical decimal u64 string; isAccountSid exposes the narrower check principal configuration requires: a canonical S-1-5-21 user SID with four sub-authorities or S-1-5-80 service SID with five. decodeOpenPayload reads an OPEN payload as the literal bytes null (an anonymous client) or one peer in strict JSON. The stdio mux between a broker and its frontend is wire-identical to the shipped Windows sidecar: u32 length | u8 kind | u64 conn | payload, big-endian, length counting kind, conn and payload (9 to 9 + 16 MiB, so a full 16 MiB payload fits); READY (conn 0, empty), OPEN, FRAME (1 byte to 16 MiB) and CLOSE (empty). encodeMuxMessage writes one; MuxDecoder reassembles them from arbitrary chunks, refuses a bad length, kind or kind rule from the shortest prefix that shows it (MUX_LENGTH, MUX_KIND, MUX_READY, MUX_FRAME, MUX_CLOSE) and allocates a payload only as it arrives. Golden vectors built as the sidecar's emit() builds them pin the wire, and the Windows host package's tests run the real sidecar against this codec: its READY, OPEN, FRAME and CLOSE decode here, its OPEN peer passes decodeOpenPayload, and FRAME and CLOSE written by encodeMuxMessage reach its clients. Refusals are BrokerWireError with fixed messages, never quoting the input.

primitives.name: Credential broker Linux socket frontend
primitives.desc: Rust binary orynq-socket-frontend (packages/broker/native), the Linux counterpart of the Windows named-pipe sidecar: it owns the broker's Unix socket and hands {connId, peer, frame} to its Node parent over the core broker-wire stdio mux, never parsing a frame or JSON. It refuses to start unless it can identify its own end of a socket pair as it would any peer (SO_PEERPIDFD, and PIDFD_GET_INFO's cgroup id from Linux 6.13 resolved under the cgroup2 hierarchy at /sys/fs/cgroup), so a host short of either never serves on a /proc read alone, or when the socket path exists and is not a stale socket of its own account (a live one is 'in use'); it binds, sets the --mode (0600 by default, read and write bits including the owner's) before listen() so no client meets a umask-made mode, and verifies the path still holds the socket bind() made (its type, device and inode; fchmodat succeeds only on a file this account owns). Each connection's peer is the kernel's: SO_PEERCRED uid and gid, and the cgroup v2 path of the process SO_PEERPIDFD names, read from /proc/<pid>/cgroup only while PIDFD_GET_INFO shows the same live pid before and after, and bound to the cgroup id it reports by the inode of that cgroup's directory (unit tests reap the peer, or move it to another cgroup, between the reads through a test-only hook and see it refused); a connector that is gone opens as null. It admits at most 32 connections per peer (uid, gid, cgroup; every unidentified client together is one peer), 128 per uid across its gids and cgroups, which the account can multiply, and in all 1,024 or RLIMIT_NOFILE less the 64 descriptors it keeps, whichever is lower (it refuses to start when that leaves none, since subordinate uids let one account outgrow any per-uid ceiling); it holds at most one 16 MiB frame of request bytes per peer, 64 MiB per uid and 256 MiB in all (every unidentified client together is one peer and one uid), each request reserving its announced length from its peer's, its uid's and the total share in that order before its body is read and releasing it once written to stdout, so a client that announces a length and stalls blocks only its own peer and another cgroup of its uid, such as another agent session, is served at once (a unit test stalls 4 x 16 MiB in one cgroup and reserves 16 MiB in another; where a cgroup is delegated the binary forwards the other cgroup's request at once); takes frames of 1 byte to 16 MiB, reads one request at a time straight into the FRAME message that carries it to the parent, so it holds one copy, and reads nothing more until that request is answered (a byte that arrives first closes the connection unread), answers a client that half-closes after its request (no idle clock runs while a request does, so such a connection keeps its slot until B answers or closes it), closes after --idle-secs (300 by default, 1 to 86,400: it refuses to start outside them, since a deadline past its clock's range panicked every connection after its OPEN and before its CLOSE) without a request while none runs, restarting when a reply drains, and closes one whose reply does not drain in that time; it exits 2 on any parent message but a 1-byte-to-16-MiB FRAME or an empty CLOSE, and on stdin EOF it removes its socket only while the path holds that socket (type, device and inode), so a socket another frontend has since bound there, or a file that reuses the inode number, stays and exits 0. Its encoder is the sidecar's emit() and is held to core's golden vectors.

primitives.name: Credential broker
primitives.desc: Private package @fluxpointstudios/orynq-sdk-broker, slice 1a of docs/architecture/credential-broker.md in progress. parseJsonPayload decodes a request payload as UTF-8 (a byte-order mark is refused, not stripped) through core's strict JSON parser with a bound of MAX_REQUEST_VALUES = 65,536 values (the largest params any built-in rule allows hold about 50,000, which the schema tests derive from the runtime shapes and decode; schemaRules throws RangeError for an effect kind whose shapes would let a valid request hold more than the bound; an accepted 16 MiB request costs up to about 0.6 s of CPU, measured on a 2.1 GHz Xeon vCPU for 21,000 floats of about 800 digits between two subnormal-range doubles, and 0.13 to 0.33 s and at most 57 MiB above the frame for long keys, strings and 256-digit floats), so a 16 MiB frame of empty containers or object members is refused before JSON.parse builds it, and every refusal is RpcError -32700. jsonToCbor/jsonToDcbor apply the JSON-to-dCBOR profile against a declared shape and encode with conduct cborEncode (its key order): a uint whose bound fits 2^53 is a JSON integer and any other uint a canonical decimal string, text is bounded in UTF-8 bytes with an anchored pattern, bytes are lowercase hex, maps are closed (unknown, missing or null members refused), choices must match exactly one option (an overlapping schema throws), and null, booleans, floats and negatives match nothing; every refusal is -32602 with the schema path. docs/params.cddl, mandate-draft.cddl and release.cddl are the normative schemas of every §6.2 method's params, the mandate.prepare draft, the ReleaseRequest and the release record; src/schema.ts is their runtime form keyed by CDDL rule name (METHOD_PARAMS maps methods to rules), effect kinds plug into the group sockets $$intent-effect and $$release-effect (schemaRules plus the exported shape builders uint, text, bytes, literal, array, map, optional and choice register one from outside the package), and none is registered yet, so every intent.submit and release.commit is refused. test/vectors give each valid case in wire JSON and dCBOR diagnostic notation and each invalid case as a patch, and both @cbortech/cbor (CDDL, anchored .regexp per RFC 8610) and the runtime profile must reach the labelled verdict. A generated probe suite then holds the runtime shapes to the CDDL at every node of every rule (305 schema paths, about 3,000 probes): integers at min-1, min, max and max+1, texts, byte strings and arrays at the sizes around both bounds, each present member removed, an unknown member added and each literal changed; a member or choice no vector reaches gets an instance built from the runtime shape that both sides must accept first, so a bound, size, optional member or member set that drifts on either side fails the suite. In the other direction, every option of every choice the CDDL's rules reach (type and group choices and socket extensions, 29 instances) gets an instance built from the @cbortech CDDL AST that both sides must accept, so a literal, alternative or optional member that only one side has fails it too. Framing (§6.1): encodeFrame and FrameDecoder carry a uint32 big-endian length N with 1 <= N <= 16 MiB, reassemble partial reads, refuse N = 0 and oversize lengths from the header alone, and grow each payload buffer only as its bytes arrive (doubling, capped at N), so an announced length costs nothing until it is sent; decodeRequest turns one frame payload (what the Windows sidecar hands over) into one JSON-RPC 2.0 request, refusing batches, notifications, null or malformed ids, unknown members and malformed methods with -32600 and reading omitted params as {} (JSON-RPC 2.0 allows omission) and leaving any params present to the method's schema; serveConnection serves a half-open Node Duplex (Unix sockets) one request at a time, closes on a framing error, on any byte that arrives before the reply has drained, and after 300 s without a completed request or a drained reply (the clock restarts when a reply is queued and again when it drains, so a reply the client never reads cannot pin the connection; partial frames do not restart it; a running request stops it), answers a request whose client half-closed after sending it and then closes, resolves 'reset' on any stream error such as a client vanishing mid-reply, answers RpcError from the table with the request id (null when undecodable), and rejects only on any other handler failure or a stream that is not half-open, always with an Error (a thrown value that is not one becomes its cause, so a handler that throws 'end' cannot read as a clean close). RpcError takes code and message only from RPC_ERRORS (the JSON-RPC standard codes plus spec §6.3's -32001 to -32012: PEER_UNKNOWN, ALIAS_UNAVAILABLE, POLICY_REFUSED, DECODE_REFUSED, APPROVAL_DENIED and APPROVAL_EXPIRED at -32005, UPSTREAM_FAILED, JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE for the *_UNAVAILABLE family, LOCKED_OUT, RATE_LIMITED, INTENT_UNKNOWN, MANDATE_REFUSED, VERIFY_REFUSED; a test derives the expected table from the spec text) plus a decoder path built from schema names, so no reply quotes the request. Broker (src/broker.ts) maps a frontend's peer to a principal per §5.2 (operator by configured uid or SID; service:<name> by uid inside its unit's cgroup or by service SID; agent:<sessionId> only for the orynq-agent uid in <slice>/orynq-agent-<sessionId>.service of an open session; anything else, and an anonymous client, none), refuses a configuration that gives two principals one uid or SID or a non-canonical cgroup path, caps connections at 8 per agent session, 32 per other principal and 32 per account without one (enforced by the host), and dispatches through a method table: no principal (or an agent whose session closed) is PEER_UNKNOWN for every request, a method outside the table or the caller's access is -32601, params go through the method's CDDL rule. Served now: broker.hello ({protocol: 2, brokerId = SHA-256 of the receipt-key SPKI, receiptKey, policyHash = SHA-256 of policy.cbor, principal, sessionId for agents only, the session's mandates, verifyMode replay, journalHead {seq, hash}}), and operator-only session.open (distinct commitments from the configured registered set, else MANDATE_REFUSED naming the first unknown; a random 128-bit sessionId and unit orynq-agent-<sid>.service) and session.close (answers {sessionId, unit}, unknown is -32602). session.bound and session.closed events extend an in-memory §11 journal chain, hash = SHA-256("orynq:broker:journal:v1|" || prev || dCBOR(event)) from 32 zero bytes; persistence, the registry's revocation, validity and set checks on bound mandates, and every other method are not built. serveMux is B's side of a frontend's broker-wire stdio mux (the Linux orynq-socket-frontend or the Windows sidecar): it waits for READY, maps each OPEN's peer to a principal once (a payload outside the peer contract is reported and served as unknown; a valid peer no principal names, such as SYSTEM, is unknown without a report and counted under its own account), refuses a principal's connection past its cap with CLOSE, and the connection of a peer without a principal past its account's cap of 32 (a uid, a SID, or every anonymous or unparseable client together), since a frontend counts peers by cgroup and any account can create cgroups, and keeps it counted until the frontend's own CLOSE, answers each FRAME through answer() (the decodeRequest-plus-error-table step serveConnection also uses), drops frames and replies that cross a CLOSE, closes a connection whose handler fails with anything but an RpcError (reported), and rejects, without reading on, when the frontend breaks the protocol (speaks before READY, READY twice, a second OPEN, a FRAME or CLOSE for a connection it never opened, a second request in flight, a malformed message, output that ends inside a message). startLinuxFrontend refuses an idleSeconds outside 1 to 86,400 before spawning anything, spawns the binary with --socket, --mode and --idle-secs, rejects with the frontend's own message, or its name and exit code, if it exits before READY (a squatted path, a kernel that cannot report a peer's cgroup id), reports and kills one that breaks the protocol, and close() ends its stdin so it removes its socket and exits. startWindowsFrontend serves the Windows sidecar through that same host: it spawns it with spawnPipeFrontend from the Windows host package's ./frontend entry, so the broker never loads that package's native bindings (a test mocks the package's root entry and sees it never imported), and rejects before spawning on any option spawnPipeFrontend refuses. On Windows the real sidecar relays two requests on one connection, hands principalOf a peer with exactly the contract's keys, closes only the connection whose handler failed and reports the failure, and fails a request still running in the broker when its client closes; the Unix socket, client and stand-in frontend suites run on Linux alone. connectBroker refuses before connecting unless lstat shows a socket owned by the configured broker uid whose mode grants this account write, and every directory above it (after realpath) is owned by root or the broker and writable by neither group nor others, sticky or not (in a sticky directory another account can bind the name once the broker's socket is gone, squat it before the broker starts, or mount a filesystem that reports any owner), so only root or the broker can change the path before connect(); tests build sockets under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or the home directory, and alter the owner lstat reports to show a directory another account owns is refused; requests go one at a time, results resolve, error replies reject as BrokerReplyError {code, message, field}, and a reply for another id, a reply that is not strict JSON or a dropped connection rejects and closes the client. test-socket (pnpm test:socket, CI step broker-socket after broker-native) runs the real binary, host and client unprivileged: the peer equals process.getuid/getgid/pid and /proc/self/cgroup, unknown, out-of-unit and vanished-connector peers get PEER_UNKNOWN, 32 connections pass and the 33rd closes, idle close, stdin close removes the socket and ends the process, a squatted path is refused, the socket is created 0600 unless a mode is given, and a client pinning another uid never reaches the broker; where a cgroup is delegated to the test account it also places the test process in a real orynq-agent-<sid>.service cgroup (agent principal, 8 admitted and the 9th refused by B), answers one agent session's broker.hello at once while another session announces four 16 MiB requests and stalls, and proves B's own 32 cap against a peer the frontend counts separately, and elsewhere a test proves the delegation is refused (EROFS, EACCES or EPERM).

primitives.name: Credential broker Windows host
primitives.desc: Public package @fluxpointstudios/orynq-sdk-credential-broker-windows (win32 only), the Windows counterpart of broker-socket-frontend. orynq-pipe-frontend, a Rust sidecar, owns the broker's named pipe: first instance only, remote clients rejected, an owner-pinned DACL that grants admitted accounts no pipe-instance creation, each caller identified by impersonating it at identification level (SID, logon LUID, TS session, integrity RID), frames of 1 byte to 16 MiB, one request in flight, an idle close (300 s by default, 1 to 86,400 s) and 32 connections per peer; it hands {connId, peer, frame} to its parent over the core broker-wire stdio mux and never parses a frame. spawnPipeFrontend, exported alone at ./frontend so its caller loads no native code, spawns the sidecar with the mux on its stdin and stdout without waiting for READY, and refuses before spawning a pipe outside \\.\pipe\, an admitted SID that isAccountSid refuses and an idle period outside 1 to 86,400 s; the private broker's startWindowsFrontend serves it. connectBroker opens the pipe at identification level with exactly the rights the sidecar grants and refuses a pipe its pinned server SID does not own; sealSecret and unsealSecret wrap the sealed executor's identity under a non-exportable TPM key in the calling account's Platform Crypto Provider store; the root entry binds its DLLs through koffi on first use. orynq-service-host runs a program as a Windows service under its virtual account, and scripts/install-service.ps1 installs one with an admin-only service DACL, recovery actions and a state directory admitting only SYSTEM and the service SID. CI type-checks and lints the sidecar for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu; its pipe-level tests, against the sidecar through core's mux codec, run on Windows.

primitives.name: Receipt checkpoint primitives
primitives.desc: Shared SCALE receipt decoding, canonical certificate encodings, daemon-compatible Merkle proofs whose verifier binds the leaf index and an authenticated leaf count, deterministic census batches, bounded compact member snapshots and canonical Midnight batch-set commitments used by the public verifier, private writer and gateway proof store. Materios detailed-schema wrappers require one correctly typed key, and dcbor certificate reconstruction supports the reviewed live and legacy certificate domains without rewriting a historical checkpoint commitment genesis.

primitives.name: Authenticated Midnight block reads
primitives.desc: Composes body-root, GRANDPA and pinned-runtime proofs into network/policy-bound complete blocks. Strict-extension runtime queries authenticate the actual :code hash and the presence or proven absence of :pending_code, which a set_code block's child executes, without fetching external Wasm. Bounded contiguous ranges share verified authority paths with per-original-root cumulative transition limits while retaining the original policy identity. Ten-block execution batches reuse body-authenticated parent headers and bound encoded requests to 32 calls and 8 KiB without changing runtime or storage-proof verification. Catch-up authenticates a complete-day and author-window floor before appending, resumes the exact durable cursor and replays migrated indexes under shared per-turn HTTP bounds. Private SQLite retains observations, exact provenance and scoped commitment history.
